title: Workflow declaration
description: The shape of one workflow. A workflow is declared here as data, never inside a script. bin/workflow-spec.sh, bin/workflow-spawn.sh and bin/workflow-watch.sh read these files and hold no copy of any fact in them, so the orchestrator starts the correct agent by reading a spec instead of a human retyping parameters. Nothing in this schema names a project: the project lives in config/project.json alone.

id.description: Stable workflow id. The file must be named <id>.workflow.json; bin/workflow-spec.sh resolves it by that convention.

why.description: Why this workflow exists, in terms of the failure it prevents. Required, not optional: a workflow that cannot answer this is machinery nobody asked for.

watcher.description: The watcher whose ALERT line raises this workflow, when on is watcher-alert or threshold.

agent.description: Everything needed to spawn the right agent. bin/workflow-spec.sh <id> prints exactly this object, and bin/workflow-spawn.sh consumes it. Per the repository's CLAUDE.md a seat is started through herdr and never through an in-process agent tool, and a seat that has finished its work exits.

context_threshold_percent.description: Percent of the context window at or above which the seat runs the compaction ceremony before its next step, never mid-step. Required on every agent spec. A spec without it fails validation, because a threshold that lives in an agent's memory is not a threshold: it is a habit, and habits do not survive a handoff.

denied_tools.description: Task and Agent belong here for every seat: the repository's CLAUDE.md forbids in-process spawning, and a denial that is only written in prose is not a denial.

denied_commands.description: Exact command prefixes the seat must never run.

allowed_paths.description: Repo-relative write boundary, disjoint between seats that run at the same time. An empty array means the seat writes nothing.

gates.description: Every gate is a command with an expected result. A gate that cannot be run is not a gate. A gate that duplicates the project's own gate_command must call it rather than reimplement it.

owner_decision.description: True when the failure of this gate is a decision only the owner can take. The watcher prefixes such a line with ALERT and leaves every other line a lowercase key: prefix, so the owner hears one line only when the decision is theirs.

verified_by.description: The command a reader runs to see the exit condition for themselves.

record.description: The record this workflow emits, declared as a real JSON Schema so a validator can check an instance without knowing anything about the workflow.

emitted_to.description: state:<path> relative to config/project.json's state_dir. Records never land in the repository.

additionalProperties.description: Enforced by this meta-schema rather than left to reviewer discipline. A record schema that tolerates unknown fields lets a drifting producer pass the gate silently.
